title: The pool dry run prices an arm with no earlier record at a default run half its real cost, and the spend cap starves the arms that run last
goal: The 2026-10-08 smoke record (_cache/scratch/ST-xy5kmisr/smoke/pool-smoke.csv) estimated 23.37 USD and spent 26.62 before the cap stopped it: the opus-5-5 labels cost 15.7 USD against 7.84 estimated from DEFAULT_RUN, as the results file holds no earlier Opus record, and since the fresh arms run first and Opus among them, router, hook, the web arms and every session label never started. The dry run's estimate for an arm with no earlier record is within 25% of that arm's smoke cost (for example the newest record of an arm with the same tools, priced at the arm's own model), the estimate of the whole smoke command is within 25% of what a full run costs (the smoke's per-label costs, with the session and web labels taken from the 2026-10-08 record), and a run the cap stops leaves every planned arm label with runs, not the last labels with none (how the cap shares the runs out is a provisional gate); a test plans such a run with a fake runner and a cap below its cost and checks that every label ran

run: import subprocess,sys,re; o=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/benchmarks.py','run','pool','--arms','opus-5-5','--sample','2','--reps','1','--dry-run'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout; m=re.search(r'estimate \$([0-9.]+) in all',o); assert m and float(m.group(1))>=12, o[-300:]

gates.question: What prices one run of an arm label that has an earlier record, in the dry run estimate?
options: the mean cost of the label's runs in its newest record (what they were billed, web searches and tool-side model calls included)
the mean input and output counts of the label's newest record, priced at the list prices
gates.recommendation: the mean cost of the label's runs in its newest record (what they were billed, web searches and tool-side model calls included)
gates.answer: the mean cost of the label's runs in its newest record (what they were billed, web searches and tool-side model calls included)

the stated default run priced at the arm's own model

gates.question: How does the spend cap share runs out between arm labels and between the fresh and the session shape?
options: within a shape the labels' runs start one of each in turn, and the cap is shared between the shapes by their estimated spend over what is left
a fixed share of the cap for each label, in proportion to its estimate
the task order as it was, with the last part of the cap held back for the last labels
gates.recommendation: within a shape the labels' runs start one of each in turn, and the cap is shared between the shapes by their estimated spend over what is left
gates.answer: within a shape the labels' runs start one of each in turn, and the cap is shared between the shapes by their estimated spend over what is left

gates.question: In which Haiku 5.5 price tier is a run priced when its price comes from counts and not from a billed cost?

the tier of the run's whole input counted as one request
